text: The parser logs the field name "oai_citation" when an export contains an unresolved citation object. Our incident report records that field so the publishing team can search the affected files and replace the objects with working references.
The serializer test uses `{"oai_citation": "sample", "index": 2}` as its input object. The assertion checks that the object becomes a readable link rather than raw JSON in the exported article.

The support ticket reproduces ":contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}" as the text readers saw beside the chart. The export skipped its citation-resolution step, leaving the internal reference visible in the downloaded report.

To test the renderer, pass `:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}` as a sample marker. The renderer should display an unresolved-reference warning until the test supplies a source URL. This is an input example in the developer guide.

The export diagnosis identifies "[oaicite:2]" as an unresolved citation token. Engineers traced it to the second record in the source list and restored the missing destination before republishing the repayment notice.

The publishing workshop shows the broken token `[oaicite:11]` beside the corrected reference so editors can recognize this failure. Participants then open the source list and check that the exported link leads to the same document.
